title: I'd echo everything everyone's said about Danny V. So many kids grew up reading him, and hoping their teams would get in his stories—and some of us wound up going from there to working alongside him. Covering high schools, seeing Danny V. at a game signaled it was a big one. But the bigger thing is really the reason why I think it sucks that more young reporters now don't cover high schools before covering college or the pros. Danny got stories because he built real relationships with people, and they trusted him to tell their stories. If Danny beat you on something, that was usually why, and seeing it showed a lot of us the importance of creating a network of people in a way that could only be done through real, human interaction (and not just calling for a box score). And as for his impact, I saw someone say on here that it'd be hard to count the number of refrigerators his byline was stuck to over the years. I think that says a lot about the difference he made for people. RIP, my friend. Best to all who loved him.
